posts.line: Police tear-gas opposition leaders *today*. The CS vows 'tough action' on violence tomorrow. Sawa.
posts.fact: Oct 12: police tear-gassed DCP leaders storming a station; same day CS Kindiki vowed action on violence.

posts.message: Tear gas against opposition leaders, then a vow to punish political violence sponsors, same day.

posts.caption:
Tear gas one day. Tough talk the next. We've seen this script before, every election season. Who's really sponsoring political violence in Kenya? Verify before you share, and send this to someone still asking.

#JuaKesho #SautiYaMwananchi

critic.note: The irony lands hard, but 'who sponsors this?' deflates into a generic election-season complaint—sharpen it with a specific detail (a name, a pattern, a number) that makes the hypocrisy undeniable, not just suspected.

scripts.radio: Habari, hii ni Jua Kesho, mimi ni Jua. This week, let's talk about who's paying and who's not. Kenyans are keeping their end of the bargain — electricity bills paid on time. But the state? It owes Kenya Power Sh7.35 billion, unpaid, as of October 2026. Meanwhile at HELB, the man in charge of student loans has never needed one himself — and students are still waiting on theirs. Now, a fact worth repeating: M-Pesa is not British. It was built, tested, and launched right here in Kenya, in 2007. Say it with your chest. And speaking of homegrown wins — M-KOPA, a Kenyan startup, now powers over five million homes across Africa with pay-as-you-go solar. Kenyan innovation lighting up a continent. But let's zoom out. 2027 is closer than you think. Five things are quietly moving us there: the election date, fixed by law; boundary reviews, overdue, deciding how much your vote counts; party primaries, the real gatekeepers to your ballot; the budget calendar, set every February 15th before any Finance Bill; and us, Jua Kesho, building a record of promises now, so 2027 is judged on receipts. Stay informed. Stay ready. Kwa Kiswahili: Wakenya wanalipa umeme kwa wakati, lakini serikali inadaiwa mabilioni na Kenya Power. M-Pesa ilizaliwa Kenya, si Uingereza. M-KOPA, kampuni ya Kikenya, inawasha nyumba milioni tano Afrika. Na njia ya 2027 inaanza sasa — tarehe ya uchaguzi, mipaka ya kura, chaguzi za ndani za vyama, na bajeti ya taifa. Jua Kesho inarekodi ahadi zote, ili tuwe tayari.
scripts.voice_note: Niaje, ni Jua hapa. Quick one today. Kenya Power says Kenyans are paying their electricity bills on time, good for us. But guess who's not paying? The government — Sh7.35 billion owed, as of this October. Make that make sense. Also, quick myth-bust: next time someone says M-Pesa is British, tell them no, it was built, tested and launched right here in Kenya back in 2007. We did that. Something else to watch: a Kenyan startup, M-KOPA, is now powering over five million homes across Africa with solar, pay as you go. That's us exporting solutions, not just importing problems. Last thing, 2027 isn't far. The election date is fixed by law, second Tuesday of August. But boundaries, party primaries, and the budget calendar are moving right now, quietly, and they'll decide a lot. We're tracking it all at Jua Kesho, building receipts so promises don't just disappear. That's your sixty seconds. Tuonane next week.

Two: your constituency boundaries, overdue for review, deciding how much your vote counts. Three: party primaries, the real test before the ballot.
